key_insight: LUCQUE introduces a large, comprehensively annotated lung cancer screening dataset from Québec. It aims to make evaluation of screening AI more reproducible, comparable, and independent.
problem_solved: AI screening tools are often evaluated using private or fragmented public datasets with inconsistent clinical information and expert nodule annotations, making reliable comparisons difficult.
method: Build a dataset from low-dose CT lung cancer screening in Québec.
Provide comprehensive annotations to address gaps in existing evaluation datasets.
Support more consistent AI assessment; dataset size, access conditions, and validation details are not available in the supplied abstract excerpt.
impact: LUCQUE could help AI/ML practitioners benchmark lung cancer screening tools more consistently and assess their reliability. The supplied excerpt does not report quantitative results.
visual_elements: Québec map linked to a low-dose CT scanner icon to show the dataset's origin.
Lung CT illustration with highlighted nodules to represent expert annotations.
Pipeline diagram: screening scans → annotated dataset → AI evaluation.
Comparison graphic contrasting fragmented datasets with a unified evaluation resource.
paper_title: LUCQUE: A lung cancer screening dataset from Québec for reliable AI evaluation
paper_authors: Johanna Topalis, Yannick Lemaréchal, Gabriel Couture, Hanife Ersay, Loran Nas
